account:
Today I have kept my appointments, though some official business has produced little information. At the mill I saw 88 hay bales and 80 emeralds, with a price of two emeralds per bale. That verifies stock and price, not grain quality or delivery records; the inspection remains incomplete. At my thirteen o'clock office appointment the secretary confirmed that no council letters had arrived.

The unusual thing is the repeated interest in the great hall. The innkeeper repeatedly asked the secretary to confirm my inspection at eighteen today and said the hall would be ready. I have agreed to meet the builder at seventeen fifty-five. This could simply be preparation for a normal inspection, but I do not yet know what is being prepared or why the timing matters so much.

There are also vague reports about a bridge or port change. Townsfolk 11 associated such talk at the bakery with the baker, innkeeper, and neighbour. That is hearsay, not proof of a proposal or of anyone organizing one. The secretary says the baker could name neither a specific proposal nor its proposer and had only vague rumours. Yesterday's enquiries likewise produced no confirmed quay problem. None of this establishes that nothing is happening; it only means I have not verified anything.

I am now at the dockside cottage for my scheduled tea with neighbour. I have asked how they are and what has been happening around the docks, but have not yet heard an answer. My best assessment is that there may be informal discussion or preparations I have not been told about, possibly connected to the quay or the hall, but I cannot yet connect those threads or say what they are for. I should listen without treating suspicion as fact, return for sixteen-thirty office hours, and keep the agreed hall inspection.
